Both symbols are set in bold italic, with the (2006.01) edition indicator in superscript. C07C 317/24 covers sulfones whose sulfone-bearing carbon skeleton is further substituted by halogen; A01N 41/10 covers biocides containing sulfone or sulfoxide groups. Consistent with a chlorinated methylsulfonyl aromatic herbicide.

paragraphs.zh: Es wird eine thermodynamisch stabile Kristallmodifikation des herbiziden Wirkstoffs 2-({2-Chlor-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluorethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl) cyclohexan-1,3-dion (Tembotrione) beschrieben. Diese thermodynamisch stabile Kristallmodifikation weist besondere Vorteile in der Stabilität von Suspensionformulierungen auf.
paragraphs.en: A thermodynamically stable crystal modification of the herbicidal active ingredient 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl) cyclohexane-1,3-dione (tembotrione) is described. This thermodynamically stable crystal modification shows particular advantages in the stability of suspension formulations.
paragraphs.notes: Abstract, set in two justified columns under the (57) code; the first column ends mid-word at 'be-' and the sentence completes with 'schrieben' at the top of the second column. HYPHENATION REPAIRED at five line breaks, all of them typographic: 'Kristall-modifikation' to 'Kristallmodifikation', 'phe-nyl' to 'phenyl', 'be-schrieben' to 'beschrieben', 'Kristallmodi-fikation' to 'Kristallmodifikation', 'Sus-pensionformulierungen' to 'Suspensionformulierungen'. HYPHENS KEPT because they are part of the name: '2-Chlor-' at the end of line 2 (the locant separator before 4-(methylsulfonyl)), '2,2,2-' at the end of line 3, and '1,3-dion'. AS PRINTED, NOT CORRECTED: there is a space between 'carbonyl)' and 'cyclohexan-1,3-dion' in the abstract, where the title at (54) prints the same name closed up with no space; and the abstract prints 'Suspensionformulierungen', where standard German would be 'Suspensionsformulierungen'. Both are left exactly as printed. This is the first place the common name Tembotrione is tied to the systematic name.
